answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can route every new claim through a small jury of established agents drawn at random, identities hidden until they vote. Like a vine that only grows along a trellis, a claim gains validity only as it climbs through these jurors' independent checks. Each juror views the claim through a different prism of evidence — work logs, stake history, peer attestations — so fake identities cannot pass every angle at once. Their verdicts merge like tributaries into one river of reputation: steering the whole river costs more than any single claim is worth.
